topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture's core themes on cancer evolution and the tumor microenvironment alongside the intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Clonal selection and non-mutational mechanisms of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how genetic mutations and epigenetic changes confer selective fitness advantages that drive Darwinian clonal evolution in tissues.

topics.label: Stemness and cell-of-origin models in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tissue hierarchies, stem cell properties, and specific cells of origin influence tumor initiation and propagation.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promotion, chronic inflammation, and stromal support
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how external factors, inflammatory signaling, and stromal interactions create permissive conditions that enable malignant outgrowth and sustain established tumors.

topics.label: Experimental and computational methods for investigating tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the genomic sequencing, spatial profiling technologies, and computational modeling approaches used to analyze tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental interactions.

topics.label: Integrated multifactorial model of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It synthesizes how genetic mutations, cell-of-origin characteristics, transcriptional plasticity, and microenvironmental pressures converge to drive cancer progression.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of therapy
topics.groupedBecause: It closes the lecture and outlines the topic for the subsequent session.
